pointers.sentence: `ModelAdmin.delete_view` is under `csrf_protect`, and runs a request whose method is not safe inside `atomic` on the database the router gives for writing the model, so a confirmed delete's collection, log and delete run in one transaction (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.delete_view`).
`ModelAdmin._delete_view` does the work, in this order (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._delete_view`):

Its default calls the function of that name in `django.contrib.admin.utils`, which collects the objects with a `NestedObjects` on the database the router gives for writing them, and returns four values: the tree of what would be deleted, as nested lists of strings; the number of each model's objects, under its plural verbose name; the verbose names of the models the user may not delete; and the protected objects, as strings (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:get_deleted_objects`).
Then it calls `Collector.collect`, and catches `ProtectedError` and `RestrictedError` into its set of protected objects (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:NestedObjects.collect`).

A cascade's nested call is this method too, so a `ProtectedError`, raised by the call whose rows a protected relation points at, ends only that call, and the collection goes on; a `RestrictedError` comes only from the outermost call, once everything is collected (`django/db/models/deletion.py:CASCADE`, `django/db/models/deletion.py:Collector.collect`).

A cascade's nested call is this method too, so a `ProtectedError`, raised by the call whose rows a protected relation points at, ends only that call, and the collection goes on; a `RestrictedError` comes only from the outermost call, once everything is collected (`django/db/models/deletion.py:CASCADE`, `django/db/models/deletion.py:Collector.collect`).

`NestedObjects.related_objects` adds `QuerySet.select_related` of the field, so each row arrives, whole, with the object the edge is read from (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:NestedObjects.related_objects`).

`NestedObjects.nested` walks the edges from the roots, depth first, and gives each object once, followed by a list of its children if it has any (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:NestedObjects.nested`).

`ModelAdmin.render_delete_form` renders `"admin/delete_confirmation.html"`, unless the model or its application has its own, or `ModelAdmin.delete_confirmation_template` names one ([The admin's templates and media](templates.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.render_delete_form`).

The template shows the models the user may not delete; failing those, the protected objects; failing those, the summary, the tree and a form that posts `"post"` (`django/contrib/admin/templates/admin/delete_confirmation.html`).
The lists are drawn by `truncated_unordered_list`, given `BaseModelAdmin.delete_confirmation_max_display` (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_filters.py:truncated_unordered_list`).
The documentation calls it purely a display setting, which does not change what is fetched (`docs/ref/contrib/admin/index.txt`).

Then `ModelAdmin.log_deletions` writes the log's row, first, as its docstring requires ([The log and the history: `LogEntry` and `history_view`](log.md)), and `ModelAdmin.delete_model` calls `Model.delete`, which collects again with an ordinary collector; `ModelAdmin.delete_queryset` is its counterpart for `delete_selected` (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.delete_model`).
The documentation warns that an override of `delete_model` must still delete: it is not for a veto (`docs/ref/contrib/admin/index.txt`).

Otherwise it adds "The ship “Endeavour” was deleted successfully." at `SUCCESS`, and redirects to the change list, keeping the preserved filters, if the user may change the model's objects, and to the index if not (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.response_delete`). nora, allowed to view and delete voyages but not to change them, was sent to /admin/.
